title: Meal Credit Values, Daily Meal Limit and Overage Meal Prices - Dining Plan
content:
Every Dining Plan meal is valued in meal credits according to its meal period, and a resident meal served when no credits remain is priced at the plan's overage meal price. The chart below gives these figures for every plan of the Dining Plan.

## Credits redeemed per meal (all six plans)

| Meal period | Meal credits redeemed per meal |
|---|---|
| Breakfast | 0.5 |
| Lunch | 1.0 |
| Dinner | 1.0 |
| Brunch | 1.0 |

The same values apply on the Dining 10, 15, 30, 45 and 60 Meal Plans and the Dining Full Board Plan.

## Daily meal limit and bistro credit value (all six plans)

| Figure | Value on every plan |
|---|---|
| Maximum meals redeemed per person per day | 3 meals |
| Bistro purchase value one meal credit covers (any excess is charged) | 12.50 US dollars per credit |

## Overage meal price by plan

The overage meal price is the price of a resident meal when no credits remain, in US dollars per meal.

| Plan | Overage meal price (USD per meal) |
|---|---|
| Dining 10 Meal Plan | 17.25 |
| Dining 15 Meal Plan | 16.75 |
| Dining 30 Meal Plan | 16.25 |
| Dining 45 Meal Plan | 15.75 |
| Dining 60 Meal Plan | 15.25 |
| Dining Full Board Plan | 14.75 |

## Worked readings of the chart (hypothetical meals)

- A resident who takes breakfast and dinner on one day redeems 0.5 credit and 1.0 credit, 1.5 credits in total for the day.
- A resident who takes breakfast, lunch and dinner on one day redeems 2.5 credits and has reached the limit of 3 meals for that day.
- Two breakfasts are worth one credit between them, the same as a single lunch or a single dinner.
- A bistro purchase of exactly 25.00 US dollars is covered by two credits of 12.50 US dollars each, leaving nothing in excess.
- On the Dining 30 Meal Plan a resident meal priced at the overage meal price costs 16.25 US dollars; on the Dining Full Board Plan the same meal costs 14.75 US dollars.
